label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Spooky turns      (Halloween spooky)
reports.comment:
quick: Good spooky turns high up (Halloween spooky). Parking to 2000m 5-10cm, 2000m to alp 15-50cm in immediate lees. Surprisingly good skiing up high. Minimal core shots on the ski out.
South slopes pretty bare. Just good enough.

reports.title: Wawa ridge
reports.comment: quick: Short walk up Wawa to dig a pit. Snow was heavy and supportive. Some fresh wind slabs forming at treeline. We did not go into the alpine but observed significant cornice growth on neighboring peaks and blowing snow in the moderate range at ridge top. Kicked on some small cornices in immediate lees, average 20 - 50cm. Stubborn in the deeper spots, reactive in the thinner spots / snowpack: Sh…

reports.title: Grizzly Glades
reports.comment: quick: HS of 45 cm on SE aspect at 2350m. Knife-hard crust at ground level with low-density settled storm snow on top. Small (1mm) facets observed on the crust, but compression test showed no results. Ski penetration 10 cm on fast snow. Decent skiing in low-angle meadow terrain. Alpine zones wind-stripped to rock during the storm. Intermittent squalls throughout the day. Below 2100m, snow became s…

reports.title: Healy Pass Conditions
reports.comment: quick: Early season tour up to Healy Pass today. Snow is remarkably good near the pass. 60cm HS. Good firm base at 40cm with 20cm light dry powder on top. Snowpack is well-consolidated. Snowed steadily all day, -4º. Thin near trailhead (5cm), but increases in depth with elevation. Trail is in great shape.

reports.title: Sunshine meadows walk
reports.comment: quick: Went for an early season walk to get the legs moving. Snow conditions were quite nice. Snow felt supportive under our skin track. Little to no wind down in the meadows for most of the day. Open Alpine slopes are still quite bare and wind blown

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows - Strawberry SlackCountry
reports.comment: quick: The strong winds forecasted were not noticed at TL/Subalpine. Some Light/Mod snow transport observed from neighbouring ridges.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge/Monarch Viewpoint
reports.comment: quick: Saw no avalanche activity. Thin early season snowpack, but enough to have some decent skiing in powder without hitting any rocks.

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good early season skiing in the alpine. Conditions seem stable.

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good early season skiing in the alpine. Conditions seem stable.

reports.title: Wawa Hill
reports.comment: quick: Decent exploratory cruise up Wawa Hill(?) between Twin Cairns and Wawa Ridge proper. Dug a pit 60cm down to base on Southeast Slope around 2,400m. Got through all 30 full taps with no result. 12-18cm of unconsolidated fluff on top of a fairly well baked 45cm with no major layers other than the direct ground interface. Cool temps but not frigid, higher wind in alpine but not bad through tree…

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: Light fluffy snow, about 20 cm.  Not wind effected, fairly calm day.  Did hit a few rocks, but less than expected..  Didn't see any avalanche activity in the area.  Was expecting cold weather, but probably warmed up to something like -5C.

reports.title: Twin Cairns Wind Slab
reports.comment: quick: Approached the NE fast of Twin Cairns. Did a hand shear test on the surface prior to ascending up the steep face, 10cm of fresh wind slab with more wind and snow blowing. Cracks initiated from skier weight. Bailed off to mellow slopes.

reports.title: Wawa Hump
reports.comment: quick: Practicing companion rescue at the bottom of wawa hump. We noticed snow transport accompanied by moderate S SW winds, much so that our tracks from 2 hours earlier were starting to fill in. We noticed cracking across fresh windslabs in mellow terrain.

reports.title: Sunshine Goat's Eye Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: The main concerns identified in the snowpit are the November 22 facet layer located in the middle of the snowpack and some rounding facets near the base of the snowpack. Test results were in the moderate to hard range, but recent avalanches show that these layers are currently quite reactive, especially where they are accompanied by wind loading or impacted by cornice failures.  Warming …

reports.title: Wawa Bowl
reports.comment: avalanche: No reactions cutting across Wawa Bowl. A whumph signalled the release from rocks above. Able to ski out of the slide path safely / weather: Was not pouring rain. Cannot deselect

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry Pit
reports.comment:
quick: Today we toured out behind sunshine for a quick and dirty layer ID with testing bonding of new storm snow.

In the top of the snowpack (162cm - 114cm), we were seeing fist to 4F+ DFs, with evidence of graupel and Iregular crystals as SF, with mid pack being pencil rounding grains further down (114cm - 59cm) to a decomposing crust at 59cm. 


As it was getting late, we only had time for two …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Skied Healy Pass and the surrounding knobs. We noticed some wumphing and settling on windslabs at ridgeline. Snowpack was probing 160-170cm deep at 2400m, with a noticeable crust 110cm below surface.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured up from the Sunshine parking lot to the ridge behind the Wawa Chair. Skied back down to the parking area. The snowpack felt generally supportive with no signs of instability—no whumpfing or cracking observed. There was some minor wind drifting along the ridge, but no significant snow transport or slab formation noted.

reports.title: Healy to Wawa
reports.comment: quick: Skinned up Healy cr trail to Wawa ridge via Simpsons pass. No whomping noted and slopes seemed stable. Stayed off high angled open slopes. Observed small slab avalanche that appeared skier triggered on Wawa ridge but bowl was stable and skied well

reports.title: Size 1 Rock Isle Lake
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote triggered a size 1 on the shoreline of Rock Isle Lake. Undercut a loaded slope in flat light. 10m propagation abut 5m above me on the slope. Upon examination, 4-6mm surface hoar crystals below the 20cm fist storm slab.

reports.title: Simpson Pass Trees
reports.comment:
quick: Toured in the Simpson Pass and Healy area from Sunshine. Great powder riding in areas protected from wind and in the trees.

Rider triggered accidental size 1 avalanche in open trees on a convex roll around 30 degrees on a West aspect. No rider involvement. Loose storm snow slid on the surface hoar layer. Crown was 10m wide and 20cm to 40cm deep, ran 15m-25m.

Observed cracking in the new s…

reports.title: Looking for Surface Hoar
reports.comment:
snowpack: ECT N16 and N28. N16 failed with resistance 30 cm down, no propagation. N28 failed 35 cm down on what we suspect is the Jan 3 surface hoar layer, resistant and no propagation. Snow was stiff, facets on the bottom 30cm of the snowpack. 

We heard whumpfing on our exit out about 500m from where we dug the pit. We suspect the surface hoar layer is still active in isolated terrain within the…

reports.title: Size 1.5 Bear Spirit Approach
reports.comment: avalanche: Encountered size 1.5 on Bear Spirit trail at approx. 15:30PM. Had heard avalanches from 13:00-15:00 while climbing at the Bear Spirit falls. Released at ground, ran a roughly 50m path, arresting at the creek bed. Debris field was about 10m across. Small trees visible in the debris.

reports.title: Quartz Hill Avalanche
reports.comment:
avalanche: Attempted to ski cut this convex roll, but did not see any results or shooting cracks. Upon skiing the convex roll, it avalanched a Size 1 Persistent Slab and propagated 20-25m with a 80-100cm crown line, ran about 5 metres before the slope angle prevented it from going further.

Sunny, blue bird day with moderate winds in the morning increasing to strong towards noon, suspected culprit…

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment:
quick: Approach: ~45 min
-17 C at car park. Good travel on approach snow slopes with a decent trail kicked in. Higher up snowpack became much more supportive, crampons useful on the upper steeper sections. First few meters delaminated hollow kicks and tools. Marginal screws in snicey ice. ~15m up had a settlement where ice on the rhs collapsed and fell close to belayer, not climber induced and bef…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment: avalanche: Toured up Quartz ridge via its northern aspect. High winds coming from the west. Found some sheltered, lower angle slopes from the saddle between Quartz Hill and Quartz Ridge. Observed this debris on route back to Sunshine.

reports.title: Bourgeau 9
reports.comment:
quick: Skied Bourgeau 9 above the waterfall today. Travel was fast and easy to the ridge, ridge up was heavily scoured and involved a mix of booting and skinning due to exposed rocks.

The upper lower angle part of the face was atrocious skiing on pencil sastrugi and old windslab.

Entering the main slope there was some new and touchy cornice(up to 30cm) with 5-10 of fist to 4F snow on the slope b…

reports.title: Grizzly Glades
reports.comment:
quick: 10-15 cm of near surface facets with a supportive midpack made for good skiing on all aspects in open trees. Spotty sun crust on steep solars rolls. Below 1850m found a lot of tree bombs had wrecked the snow.  The alpine was hooky wind slab to sastrugi. Light snow all afternoon but only added up to a 1-2 cm.

Observed a size 1.5 dry loose natural come out of extreme East facing high alpine …

reports.title: Citadel Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Long walk without any of my followers out to Citadel peak. 

Numerous whumpfs on buried surface hoar down an average of 15cm under old snow. This was isolated to creek walls and lake shores, anything not near a water source didn’t have this layer. 

Summit ridge of Citadel had some fresh and reactive windslabs no deeper than 5cm but actively building with trace snow and light winds througho…

reports.title: Mt Brent drainage, Surfy facets
reports.comment: quick: The snow pack in the area was shallower than else where in the Rockies 90-130cm at treeline.  The tempature crust ended at 1750m and found 20-30 cm of sugary facets sitting on a supportive midpack. Around a few boulders in shallower spots the facets go to ground. Great skiing on the way down in wind protected areas.  Tougher skinning slipping backwards in the facets.

The tempature crust ended at 1750m and found 20-30 cm of sugary facets sitting on a supportive midpack. Around a few boulders in shallower spots the facets go to ground. reports.title: Little  Bourgeau via north ridge
reports.comment:
quick: It doesn’t have to be fun, to be fun.

We found a mixed bag from facets to crusts and smoo of all kinds. Challenging gaining the ridge in crusty fascets and ski crampons were necessary as were several boot packs. Everything stayed put and we felt good about stability, but the skiing was of the survival variety. (One gully before the ridge was a bit spicy)
This was a “once and never again” o…

reports.title: Massive Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Traversed from Bourgeau lake towards massive mountain over several ridges. North aspects in the alpine had some soft wind slabs that had started to faceted out which made for good drought skiing, North aspects at treeline still had good powder. Below 1800m found spring like corn snow out the creek which was in great condition. Bourgeau trail would not be great to ski out. Found small surfac…

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment:
quick: SH investigation 
260103 active and reactive to CTH21 sudden planar down 33cm. / snowpack: Pit Dug in sunshine Backcountry on a cross loaded 25 deg slope with wind loading. Sparse trees. Jan 3 SH is still reactive and is the main layer of concern.

reports.title: Jan 3 still reactive in tests
reports.comment:
quick: Skied south aspects down FTC col, finding crusty skiing where terrain is angled more towards sun. In the afternoon lapped East and Northeast aspects around Wawa bowl with a couple other parties in the area and found great skiing, ~20-25cm of fist over the Jan 24th layer, midpack progressively resistant going from 4-finger to pencil resistance.

Digging a test pit in a sheltered surface hoar…

reports.title: Solar apects vs not solar
reports.comment:
quick: Did a circumnavigation from Twin Cairns to Quartz Ridge having a look at the Monarch on the way, seeing different aspects from morning to afternoon. 

Good Skiing on NE, E and N aspects finding from 10cm to 25cm of fist snow on top of the last layer. We found some dry loose not propagating to size 1 on steeper open tree areas.

On SW, S and SE aspects, from TL to BTL, we found a crust varyi…

reports.title: Twin Cairns + Meadows
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing down the west facing slope of the cairns from the top. Powder mostly, some crusts.
Then snow-kiting in the meadows was fantastic with ~15cm of powder.

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: We went for a mellow tour out to Quartz Ridge this morning and early afternoon. Leaving the boundary, the skies were mostly clear with some scattered cloud and winds were light out of the SW. 

Travel was easy, 5cm fist snow on top of settled mid pack, scoured conditions once at ridge top. 

By midday, the skies were completely overcast, and snow began to fly at 1215. Winds were light from …

reports.title: Quartz Hill Expedition
reports.comment:
snowpack: Aimed for the summit of Quartz Hill via the North Ridge. Opted for conservative terrain due to a visible wind slab at higher elevations (2500 - summit).

Weather:
Temperature: -13 degrees.
Light wind from the SW carried thin cloud.
Varied from full sun to full cloud.
Signs of fresh snow from previous 48 hours.

Riding conditions: Good riding conditions.  Recent storm brought in 15cm of d…

reports.title: Wind Effect on Wawa
reports.comment:
quick: Went to Wawa ridge today and noticed an inversion - it was significantly warmer as we got higher, to the point that there was a bit of pinwheeling when we were near the top of the ridge. 

We noticed some wind-affected snow, though some of the cornices on the ridge were from before the new snow. 

I tested a small cornice on a small roll heading up the ridge, and the new snow fell off the h…

reports.title: Bourgeau 9
reports.comment: quick: Great conditions on BG today!  2100-2400m 15-20 of fist snow overlying a supportive MFCR making for good travel with out having to be too concerned for things stepping down to our SH layer. As we gained ridge top very minimal blowing snow observed with light winds from the SE. We were pretty surprised to see how minimal wind affect there was working our way along the ridge line. BG10 and 9.…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge just before the rocky section
reports.comment:
quick: 20–30 cm of dense, granular snow over a firm, consolidated snowpack.

Some wind loading observed; cornices present and cracking, but not releasing significant slabs.

Snowpack passed at all three pit levels. Shovel jump on the surface layer resulted in compaction only, no propagation or collapse.

Amazing powder riding.

reports.title: Wawa ridge backside
reports.comment:
quick: We skied black towers and wizard chutes, we saw good stability in black towers but triggered several loose dry's in wizard chutes from a high ski cut on the steep slope, failing approx 20cm down on facets, entraining the new snow from earlier in the week
running 100-150m.

reports.title: Sa Outside Wild West Boundary
reports.comment: incident: Public traversing slope outside ski area boundary when it fractured 10 meters above. They were able to ski out with no involvement/injuries. Investigation of the Fracture line found facets on a crust.

reports.title: Cornice Slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Crown was spotted from a far and our party went to investigate. Stayed within our tolerance for range of hangfire. We were unable to obtain exact dimensions.

reports.title: Sunshine snowprofiles
reports.comment:
snowpack: Spend the day digging pits around the sunhine area. 

All observations were made in TL.

Started off with a full profile on a W aspect. site was wind exposed, planar, sparse trees. primary problem layer was the Jan 24th which was very prominent. Depth off the layer changed drastically from 25cm on the left side of my test wall to 60cm on the right side. Test results got harder with an in…

reports.title: Wawa Bowl and Backdoor
reports.comment: quick: Went up to Wawa Bowl during the storm on Saturday. The snow was very deep but felt stable. Insanely windy on the ridge itself. It was around -2 while skiing so perhaps that might affect the snow there and the snow coming down was wetter and heavy.

reports.title: Bourgeau 11 skier triggered avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier triggered accidental size 2.5 avalanche on Mt Bourgeau path 11, late Saturday afternoon. Unsure of the failure layer. Ran full path to the bottom of the runout.

reports.title: Just the Nub
reports.comment:
quick: Very good snow above 2300m, with ankle deep penetration and good turns.  

The storm dump was frozen stiff and supportive at 2030m, with 5 or 6cm loose snow from last night on top of it .   

We skied the "Side Door" back into bounds.   The snow started out ok and became crustier and icier as we neared Wolverine chair.  

Smalltown Djs were spinning at Goat's Eye.  Excellent Vibes.

It's st…

reports.title: Sunshine Slack Country-Rock Isle Lake
reports.comment: quick: Skiing was not great. West facing slope across from Twin Cairns was better than gully above Rock Isle Lake. / snowpack: CTM 12 RP at 45 cm. CTM 18 RP at 103 cm. ECTX. Shovel Pull on ECT Resistant Planar at 135.

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment: quick: Knee to waist deep pockets up against steep terrain and 15 cms on the approach to Spray River Falls. Sun packs a punch in the morning, we walked out with snow being blown from trees above the climb. No signs of snow instability noted during the day.

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment: quick: Dagger hanging left of the top pitch of Bourgeau Left. First pitch is a bit hollow as usual.  No signs of snow instability noted during day, slide debris is impressive.

reports.title: North side of The Monarch
reports.comment: quick: Went to check out the multiple bowls and couloirs on the north side of The Monarch, but stuck to mellow tree skiing after being struck by a size 1  Na LD at the bottom of the northern most couloir. Overall good riding conditions with ~5 cm over previous crusts at TL. Most large features had released during the previous AR event, with many crowns and debris piles still visible. / avalanche: …

reports.title: Goats eye couloir
reports.comment:
quick: the last bit is quite sketchy, skiing as well, you have to plan your route, lots of slough and windloaded in the couloir. 
triggered a size 1

reports.title: Bourgeau Lake trail
reports.comment: quick: Decided to ski up Bourgeau Lake trail. Wet, heavy, but not quite rotten snow, overall pleasant trail skiing. Turned around at 5.5km slide path, which had a large volume of debris, probably from the big March cycle, but only ran down a few meters past the summer trail. Saw some recent size 1 wet point slides farther uphill on that slide path. Slide at 2km looks like it ran all the way to the…

reports.title: Sunshine Slack Country
reports.comment: quick: Started the skin track up Sunshine from Banff Avenue at 9am. Entered the slack country behind Wawa chair and skinned up the bluff right behind the chair. Hard crust underneath wet powder. The day was mild temperatures with minimal sun exposure. No immediate signs of avalanches. Stable conditions.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment:
quick: Thick clouds overnight prevented a radiative freeze for first night in a couple weeks. It felt like it might rain at 11 but clear off in the afternoon. Inspite of the lack of freeze, Ok corn skiing was found on lower angle slopes in the morning but the snow went sticky on all solar aspects by midmorning.

There were several loose wet avalaches mostly between size 1-1.5 from below rocks/clif…

reports.title: Fatigue Mountain
reports.comment:
quick: Good freeze above 2200m.  The crust became quite burly above 2450m and it was hard to skin on steep slopes. Around rocks and thinner areas you would post hole.

 Strong  west winds and convective flurries over the last two days at ridge top deposited 2-3 cm on Lee aspects.  Decent soft crust skiing on solar aspects but north aspects remained firm unless they are Lee and have some powder on …

reports.title: Rock Isle lake
reports.comment: quick: Did some laps on the mound south of Rock Isle lake. Took small east ridge up and around, came down spine of ridge west of this. Avoided “funnel” valley area and stuck to low angle slope. The new snow quickly warmed up and became heavy. This new layer became wet even on north aspect and was unstable on the previously existing surface.
